tasks.title: Backend Unit Tests for NestJS Services and Controllers
tasks.description: Create comprehensive Jest unit tests covering all NestJS services (AuthService, UsersService, JobsService, MatchesService, StatsService) and their corresponding controllers. Tests will validate business logic, data transformation, error handling, and interaction with TypeORM repositories, while mocking external gRPC IA services to isolate the backend. Each test will assert correct manipulation of database entities such as table ('users') fields ('id'), ('email'), ('password_hash'), ('role') and verify that DTOs exclude sensitive data. The suite will also test validation pipes, JWT guards, and role-based access controls to ensure security constraints are enforced before any service method executes.
subtasks: Write unit tests for AuthService.validateUser that confirm successful authentication when the supplied password matches the bcrypt hash stored in table ('users') field ('password_hash') and that failure cases (wrong password or non‑existent email) throw an UnauthorizedException.

Implement unit tests for UsersController.createUser that mock the TypeORM repository for table ('users'), verify that a new record is persisted with correct values for fields ('email'), ('password_hash'), ('role'), and ensure the returned DTO omits the password hash.

Develop unit tests for JobsService.findMatchingJobs where the gRPC MatchService client is mocked to return a predefined cosine similarity score, asserting that the service correctly maps the result to a new entry in table ('matches') with fields ('match_score'), ('candidate_id'), ('job_id').

Create unit tests for StatsController.getDashboardStats that exercise the aggregation queries on table ('dashboard_stats'), confirming that total_applications, hired_count, and avg_match_score are accurately calculated for a given recruiter_id and period, and that the service throws a NotFoundException when no stats exist.

tasks.title: Backend Integration Tests for API Endpoints and Database Interactions
tasks.description: Build an integration test suite using SuperTest and an in‑memory SQLite database configured via TypeORM to validate full request‑response cycles. The suite will seed realistic data, exercise endpoints that trigger gRPC IA services (mocked), and verify persistence across all related tables. Special attention will be given to file upload handling, WebSocket event emission, and transaction rollback to guarantee data consistency. Each test will assert correct HTTP status codes, response payload shapes, and the presence of expected rows in tables such as ('cv_files'), ('candidate_skills'), ('matches'), ('applications'), and ('dashboard_stats').
subtasks: Set up an integration test harness that launches the NestJS application in test mode with a SQLite in‑memory database, runs TypeORM migrations to create all tables ('users'), ('candidate_profiles'), ('cv_files'), ('skills'), ('candidate_skills'), ('jobs'), ('job_skills'), ('matches'), ('applications'), ('dashboard_stats'), and seeds a recruiter and a candidate with known credentials for repeatable scenarios.

Write an integration test for POST /api/cv/upload that simulates a multipart/form‑data PDF upload, mocks the gRPC ParseCVService to return a fixed parsed_text and a list of skill names with scores, and asserts that a new row is inserted in table ('cv_files') with fields ('file_path'), ('parsed_text'), and that corresponding rows are created in table ('candidate_skills') linking the candidate to each skill with the supplied score.

Implement an integration test for GET /api/matches/:candidateId where the mocked gRPC MatchService returns cosine similarity scores for several jobs, verifying that the response contains match objects, that rows are persisted in table ('matches') with correct foreign keys to table ('users') and table ('jobs'), and that the match_score values fall within the expected 0‑1 range.

Create an integration test for the WebSocket gateway that after a match is persisted, listens for a 'new_match' event emitted to the candidate’s socket room, confirming that the payload includes the match ID, the job title from table ('jobs') field ('title'), and the match score from table ('matches') field ('match_score'), and that the candidate’s Redux store (via a test harness) updates accordingly.

tasks.title: Frontend Unit and Integration Tests with Jest, React Testing Library, and Cypress
tasks.description: Develop a layered testing strategy for the React frontend: unit tests with Jest and React Testing Library for isolated components, Redux Toolkit slices, and custom hooks; end‑to‑end tests with Cypress to validate user flows, real‑time WebSocket updates, and Chart.js visualisations. Tests will cover authentication, profile management, CV upload, matching dashboard, and recruiter statistics, ensuring that state changes correctly reflect data from backend tables such as ('users'), ('candidate_profiles'), ('cv_files'), ('matches'), ('applications'), and ('dashboard_stats'). Mock API calls (Axios) and gRPC‑web stubs will be used to simulate backend responses, while Cypress will exercise actual Socket.io‑client connections to assert live updates.
subtasks: Write unit tests for the auth slice reducer using Redux Toolkit's createSlice, testing that the login action correctly stores a mock JWT token (simulating an HttpOnly cookie), populates the auth state with user data drawn from table ('users') fields ('id'), ('email'), ('role'), and that the logout action clears the state and removes the token.

Develop unit tests for the CandidateProfileForm component with React Testing Library, filling inputs for full_name, phone, location, submitting the form, mocking the Axios PUT request to route ('PUT /api/users/profile'), and asserting that the Redux candidate_profiles slice updates with the new values and that a success notification appears.

Create a Cypress end‑to‑end test for the candidate journey: visit the login page, enter credentials from a fixture, confirm redirect to /candidate/dashboard, upload a mock PDF via drag‑drop, intercept the gRPC‑web ParseCVService call, verify that extracted skills are displayed in the profile, spy on the POST /api/cv/upload endpoint to ensure a new entry is logged in table ('cv_files'), and check that the matches list updates with a new row showing a match_score from table ('matches').

Implement a Cypress test for the recruiter dashboard: log in as a recruiter, establish a Socket.io connection, wait for the initial Chart.js bar chart (total applications per week) to render, then trigger a new application via the API route ('POST /api/applications'), assert that the chart’s data source reflects the incremented total_applications value from table ('dashboard_stats') for the recruiter’s ID and current period, and verify that a WebSocket 'application:updated' event is received and displayed as a toast notification.
